scenes.tts: Here is what one professor built, starting in June. The first thirty lessons took about seventeen weeks. The next one hundred seventy-three took about eight days. That is two hundred three lessons, in six courses, free for any student.

scenes.tts: When you finish a goal, move up one level. One course became a whole pre-med curriculum. Standard questions became questions that send a student back to the exact lesson that explains it.
scenes.visual: Two ladders: one course to curriculum; generic question to a question with an arrow to a lesson card.

scenes.tts: There was a catch. In one course, an AI fact-checker went through nearly thirty-five hundred claims. It found forty-nine that were flat wrong. It found four hundred fifty-three that were imprecise. Making lessons got cheap. Checking them became the job.

scenes.tts: Class opens with the room's own words. Does a dye-nee-in block prove track A is the cargo? Two say yes. Six say no. Nobody is named, and everyone learns in the first minute that the work was read. Each student also gets a short note before class on what to focus on.

scenes.tts: The real risk is lazy thinking. Slow thinking is the point. So we design the tool so it cannot think for the student. Reasoning is graded. Paste is guarded. A student who wants to skip a step writes a stuck note first, at least twenty-five words. And a human checks before anything is sent. Once the AI said a student had no activity. That student had finished.
